chapter_summary: Proverbs 29 is a sweeping chapter on authority, wisdom, justice, and the human heart. It opens with a stark warning: the person who keeps ignoring correction will be suddenly and completely destroyed. From there it moves through themes of righteous leadership, the dangers of flattery and anger, the necessity of parental discipline, and the peril of caring too much what other people think. At the heart of the chapter stands the famous verse about vision — where God's Word is not taught, the people fall apart. The chapter closes with an unflinching contrast: the just man and the unjust man are an abomination to each other, because righteousness and wickedness cannot coexist in peace.
main_lesson: Listen to correction, obey God's Word, and trust God — not people — to keep you safe.

memory_verse.kjv: The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the LORD shall be safe.
memory_verse.little_bible: Caring too much what people think is a trap. But trusting God keeps you safe.

parent_guide:
Proverbs 29 opens with one of the most sobering warnings in all of Proverbs: the person who repeatedly ignores correction will be destroyed — suddenly, and without any cure. This is not hyperbole. Scripture is honest that persistent rebellion against wisdom has consequences that grow beyond repair. For parents, this is a call to take correction seriously in the home — not as punishment-as-punishment, but as a genuine gift of love that shapes a life before it is too late.

The chapter's social vision is also striking. Righteous leadership produces a people who rejoice; wicked leadership makes people mourn. This is true in nations, churches, schools, and homes. The king who faithfully judges the poor secures his throne. These verses ground political and social ethics in something deeper than pragmatism — in the character of God, who defends the poor and hates corruption.

Verse 18 — 'Where there is no vision, the people perish' — is often misquoted as a call to organisational ambition. In context it means something far richer: where there is no prophetic Word from God, no teaching of Scripture, the people throw off restraint and scatter. This is a call to families and churches to make Scripture central. Your children need the Word of God not as an optional extra but as the frame that holds their lives together.

The chapter's emotional crescendo is verse 25: the fear of man is a snare, but trusting the LORD brings safety. Children will face peer pressure, fear of rejection, and the temptation to do wrong to please others. Help them see early that God's opinion is the one that lasts — and that trusting Him is the only truly safe place to stand.
application_for_children: This week, practise trusting God instead of worrying about what others think. When someone asks you to do wrong, say no and remember: God keeps you safe.

verses.kjv: He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.
verses.little_bible: If someone ignores correction again and again, they will be destroyed. And there will be no way to fix it.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Ignoring correction over and over leads to ruin.
verses.meaning: Repeated correction is a mercy. When a person stiffens against every warning and keeps choosing the wrong path, they move beyond the reach of help. The word 'suddenly' is significant — destruction does not always announce itself; it arrives when the window for repentance has closed. This verse is one of Scripture's most urgent arguments for responding to God's correction while you still can.
verses.prayer: God, help me listen when You correct me.
verses.discussion_question: What happens when we keep ignoring correction?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate in our children a heart that stays soft and teachable — not defensive or stubborn — when they are corrected?
verses.do_it_today: Think of a time someone tried to correct you. Did you listen? Thank that person today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child with crossed arms ignoring a wise elder who is speaking gently, a road ahead showing storm clouds, warm but serious watercolour scene

verses.kjv: When the righteous are in authority, the people rejoice: but when the wicked beareth rule, the people mourn.
verses.little_bible: When good leaders are in charge, people are happy. When evil leaders rule, people are sad.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Good leaders make everyone happy. Bad leaders make people sad.
verses.meaning: Leadership shapes the lives of everyone under it. Righteous authority — grounded in God's law, protecting the weak, punishing wrongdoing — produces flourishing and joy. Wicked authority produces fear, oppression, and grief. This verse calls children and adults alike to care about who leads and to pray for leaders who follow God.
verses.prayer: God, give us wise and good leaders.
verses.discussion_question: Why does a good leader make everyone happier?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to pray for leaders, to respect authority, and still to recognise when leadership is wrong?
verses.do_it_today: Pray for one leader today — a teacher, parent, or someone in government.
verses.illustration_prompt: A joyful crowd gathered under a banner with a kind ruler on one side, a sad mourning crowd on the other side under darkness, gentle watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: Whoso loveth wisdom rejoiceth his father: but he that keepeth company with harlots spendeth his substance.
verses.little_bible: A child who loves wisdom makes his father very happy. But a person who follows evil people wastes everything good they have.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Loving wisdom makes your dad happy. Bad friends waste your life.
verses.meaning: Wisdom and foolishness both have relational consequences. The wise child brings his father joy — the relationship is strengthened. The one who runs after sinful companions wastes not just money but life itself. The contrast is between building up and throwing away. Every child's choices affect their whole family.
verses.prayer: God, help me love wisdom and make my family proud.
verses.discussion_question: How do your choices affect your family?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children see that their personal choices are never purely personal — they affect every relationship around them?
verses.do_it_today: Do one thing today that you know will make your mum or dad genuinely proud.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child studying and smiling next to a proud father on one side, a figure surrounded by bad companions looking lost on the other, warm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The king by judgment establisheth the land: but he that receiveth gifts overthroweth it.
verses.little_bible: A king who judges fairly builds a strong country. A king who takes bribes destroys it.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Fair leaders build nations. Greedy leaders break them.
verses.meaning: Justice is the foundation of stable government. When rulers make decisions based on what is right rather than on who paid them, society is established. Bribery corrupts justice at its root — the outcome is decided before evidence is heard. God is the ultimate just Judge, and He calls all human authority to reflect that justice.
verses.prayer: God, help leaders judge fairly and not take bribes.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it wrong to pay someone to do the wrong thing?
verses.family_discussion: How do we explain bribery and corruption to children in a way that connects to God's character as the perfectly just Judge?
verses.do_it_today: Practise being fair in a game or decision today — even if it does not help you win.
verses.illustration_prompt: A king on a throne holding balanced scales with light around him on one side, a king pocketing gold while a city crumbles on the other, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: A man that flattereth his neighbour spreadeth a net for his feet.
verses.little_bible: A person who says only nice things to trick you is laying a trap. Flattery is not real kindness.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Fake compliments are traps. Real kindness tells the truth.
verses.meaning: Flattery — false or exaggerated praise meant to gain advantage — is a form of deception that harms the flatterer's target. By filling someone with false confidence or lowering their guard, the flatterer sets them up for a fall. True friendship tells the truth even when it is uncomfortable.
verses.prayer: God, help me be honest, not flattering.
verses.discussion_question: What is the difference between a compliment and flattery?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children recognise when someone is complimenting them sincerely versus using praise to manipulate them?
verses.do_it_today: Give someone a real, true compliment today — something you actually mean.
verses.illustration_prompt: A person smiling with hidden net behind their back while speaking sweetly to a neighbour, gentle warning atmosphere, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: In the transgression of an evil man there is a snare: but the righteous doth sing and rejoice.
verses.little_bible: Doing wrong traps the person who does it. But righteous people are free to sing and be glad.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Doing wrong traps you. Doing right sets you free to rejoice.
verses.meaning: Sin is never just an action — it creates a trap. The person who keeps doing wrong becomes caught in their own wrongdoing. Righteousness, by contrast, brings freedom and joy — the righteous person has nothing to hide and nothing to fear. This verse pictures moral life as either captivity or freedom.
verses.prayer: God, keep me free by helping me choose right.
verses.discussion_question: Why does doing wrong trap a person?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that sin is not just rule-breaking but a kind of bondage — and that obedience to God is genuine freedom?
verses.do_it_today: Think of something you know is wrong that you need to stop. Pray and ask God to help you.
verses.illustration_prompt: A figure caught in a net of their own making looking sad, while another figure dances and sings in bright open sunlight, watercolour contrast illustration

verses.kjv: The righteous considereth the cause of the poor: but the wicked regardeth not to know it.
verses.little_bible: A good person cares about what happens to poor people. A wicked person does not want to know.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Good people care about the poor. Wicked people ignore them.
verses.meaning: Care for the poor is not peripheral in Proverbs — it is a mark of righteousness. The righteous person actively considers the legal and social situation of the poor person; the wicked person refuses even to acknowledge the need. This verse reflects God's own heart, which throughout Scripture consistently defends and honours the poor.
verses.prayer: God, give me a heart that cares for poor people.
verses.discussion_question: How can you show you care about people who have less than you?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate in our children an active, informed compassion for the poor — not just pity but the willingness to understand and help?
verses.do_it_today: Find one way to help someone in need this week — give something, share something, or pray for someone.
verses.illustration_prompt: A kind child kneeling to help a poor child on the ground, warm light around them, while a figure walks past looking away, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Scornful men bring a city into a snare: but wise men turn away wrath.
verses.little_bible: People who mock and scorn stir up trouble for everyone. But wise people calm things down.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Mockers cause trouble. Wise people bring peace.
verses.meaning: Scornful people — those who mock correction, God, and authority — do not just harm themselves. Their attitude spreads and drags whole communities into danger and conflict. Wise people have the opposite effect: they de-escalate, speak truth gently, and divert the wrath that scorners provoke. Wisdom is a community-saving force.
verses.prayer: God, make me a peacemaker, not a trouble-stirrer.
verses.discussion_question: How can one person's bad attitude affect a whole group?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children identify when they are playing the role of the scorner in a group — and give them the tools to be peacemakers instead?
verses.do_it_today: The next time a group is arguing, try to say something calm and kind to bring peace.
verses.illustration_prompt: A mockers stirring up chaos in a crowd on one side, a wise person with hands raised gently calming the crowd on the other, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man, whether he rage or laugh, there is no rest.
verses.little_bible: When a wise person argues with a fool, nothing good happens. The fool will rage or laugh, but there is no peace.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Arguing with a fool never gives peace.
verses.meaning: Not every argument is worth having. A foolish person cannot be won by reason — they will either rage with anger or mock with laughter, but they will not listen. Wisdom sometimes means recognising when a person is not in a place to receive truth, and not wasting effort on an argument that only creates more conflict.
verses.prayer: God, give me wisdom about when to speak and when to stop.
verses.discussion_question: Is it always worth arguing with someone who will not listen?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children the wisdom of discernment — knowing when to engage, when to speak, and when to walk away from a fruitless argument?
verses.do_it_today: If someone is trying to pick a fight with you today, practise staying calm and walking away.
verses.illustration_prompt: A wise person speaking calmly to a laughing and raging fool, exhaustion and futility in the air, gentle watercolour scene with warm and cool tones

verses.kjv: The bloodthirsty hate the upright: but the just seek his soul.
verses.little_bible: People who love violence hate those who do right. But just people protect and care for the upright.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Evil people hate the good. Good people protect the good.
verses.meaning: Righteousness draws the hatred of those who are committed to evil — not because the righteous provoke them, but because goodness exposes evil by contrast. The just, however, seek the welfare and life of the upright. This verse affirms that righteousness will always be opposed by wickedness, but it also affirms that the righteous are not alone — others who love justice stand with them.
verses.prayer: God, protect me and help me stand for what is right.
verses.discussion_question: Why do you think evil people sometimes hate good people?
verses.family_discussion: How do we prepare our children for the reality that doing right can make them a target — and help them stand firm anyway?
verses.do_it_today: Stand up for a friend who is being treated unfairly today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A figure standing in light being glared at by shadows, while other people of light stand protectively beside them, watercolour scene with warm gold tones

verses.kjv: A fool uttereth all his mind: but a wise man keepeth it in till afterwards.
verses.little_bible: A foolish person says everything they think right away. A wise person waits and thinks before they speak.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Think before you speak. That is wisdom.
verses.meaning: Self-control in speech is a mark of wisdom. The fool vents every thought and emotion immediately — there is no filter, no patience, no consideration of timing or effect. The wise person holds back, considers the moment, and chooses words carefully. James echoes this exactly: 'be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath' (James 1:19).
verses.prayer: God, help me think before I speak.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it wise to think before saying everything you feel?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help children develop the emotional muscle of pausing — not suppressing feelings, but learning to choose the right time and right words?
verses.do_it_today: Before you say something today, ask yourself: 'Is this the right time? Is this the right way to say it?'
verses.illustration_prompt: A child with hand on chin thinking carefully before speaking, glowing thoughtful expression, compared to a figure blurting out words in a chaotic cloud, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: If a ruler hearken to lies, all his servants are wicked.
verses.little_bible: A ruler who listens to lies will be surrounded by wicked people. Leaders shape what is around them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A leader who believes lies gets bad helpers.
verses.meaning: Leadership determines culture. When a ruler accepts lies — whether from pride, laziness, or preference — dishonest people fill the court because they know they will be rewarded. Honest people leave or are pushed out. This verse is a warning about the power of what leaders choose to listen to and reward.
verses.prayer: God, make me someone who always loves truth.
verses.discussion_question: What happens when a leader always wants to hear good news, even if it is not true?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate in our home a culture where truth is always more welcome than flattery — where honest words are rewarded even when they are hard?
verses.do_it_today: Tell the truth to someone today even if it is a little bit uncomfortable.
verses.illustration_prompt: A king on a throne surrounded by whispering liars in shadows, honest advisors being pushed away at the edges, watercolour scene with dark and light contrast

verses.kjv: The poor and the deceitful man meet together: the LORD lighteneth both their eyes.
verses.little_bible: Poor people and dishonest people both live in this world. God gives eyesight and life to both of them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God gives life to both the poor and the dishonest.
verses.meaning: This verse is a profound statement about common grace. The poor person and the deceitful person are very different — one is a victim of circumstances, the other a maker of wrong choices — but God sustains them both with life and sight. This is not an endorsement of deceit but a declaration that God's sustaining grace extends even to those who misuse it. It also calls us to see all people as image-bearers God keeps alive.
verses.prayer: God, thank You for giving life and light to everyone.
verses.discussion_question: Why does God keep giving life even to people who do wrong?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children about God's common grace — His care for all people — while still being clear about the difference between right and wrong?
verses.do_it_today: Thank God for the gift of life and eyesight today.
verses.illustration_prompt: Sunlight falling equally on a poor child and a sneaky man, God's light shining on both from above, warm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The king that faithfully judgeth the poor, his throne shall be established for ever.
verses.little_bible: A king who judges poor people fairly will have a strong and lasting kingdom. Fairness builds lasting power.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Kings who are fair to the poor last forever.
verses.meaning: Earthly thrones built on injustice eventually fall. But the king who faithfully judges the poor — who does not exploit the vulnerable but gives them the same justice as the powerful — builds a kingdom on the firmest possible foundation. This is ultimately a picture of God's own eternal kingdom, where perfect justice reigns.
verses.prayer: God, help me always be fair to everyone.
verses.discussion_question: Why does treating the poor fairly make a kingdom strong?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that God has a special concern for justice for the poor — and that this is not political but deeply theological?
verses.do_it_today: Be fair to everyone today — especially to someone who cannot do anything for you in return.
verses.illustration_prompt: A glowing stable throne on a firm foundation, a wise king reaching down to help a poor person before the throne, warm light and peaceful watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The rod and reproof give wisdom: but a child left to himself bringeth his mother to shame.
verses.little_bible: Correction and discipline teach children wisdom. A child never corrected will cause sadness and shame.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Correction and teaching make children wise.
verses.meaning: Discipline is inseparable from wisdom formation. The 'rod' here represents firm, loving correction — not cruelty — and 'reproof' is verbal instruction and rebuke. Together they shape a child's character toward wisdom. The child left entirely to their own desires becomes a source of shame, not because they are bad but because they were never trained. Discipline is an act of love.
verses.prayer: God, help me receive correction with a thankful heart.
verses.discussion_question: Why do children need correction and discipline to grow wise?
verses.family_discussion: How do we explain to our children that discipline is love — not punishment for punishment's sake, but care for who they are becoming?
verses.do_it_today: When you are corrected today, respond with 'Thank you' — and mean it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A loving parent gently correcting a child who is listening with wide eyes, warm home setting, wise older figure in the background, soft watercolour scene

verses.kjv: When the wicked are multiplied, transgression increaseth: but the righteous shall see their fall.
verses.little_bible: When more wicked people get power, more wrong things happen. But the righteous will live to see them fall.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Evil spreads when bad people grow — but the righteous win in the end.
verses.meaning: Wickedness is socially contagious — when wicked people multiply in influence, sin multiplies with them. But the righteous are promised something: they will see the fall of the wicked. This is not a call to gloat but a reassurance that evil does not win forever. God's justice will come.
verses.prayer: God, help me trust that You will make all things right.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it important to know that evil will not win forever?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to hold onto faith and hope when it seems like bad people are winning — trusting God's justice without becoming bitter?
verses.do_it_today: Write or draw something that reminds you that God always wins in the end.
verses.illustration_prompt: A crowd of shadow figures falling while a righteous figure stands firm in golden light watching from higher ground, hopeful watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Correct thy son, and he shall give thee rest; yea, he shall give delight unto thy soul.
verses.little_bible: Discipline your child, and they will grow up to bring you peace. A well-taught child is a deep joy.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Children who are taught well bring joy to their parents.
verses.meaning: Discipline is not just about the child — it is about the whole family's future. The parent who invests the hard work of correction will one day receive the fruit: rest, delight, and a child who has grown into someone trustworthy and good. This is a long-game promise — faithfulness in parenting produces joy.
verses.prayer: God, help my parents as they train me up right.
verses.discussion_question: How does a well-taught child make their family happy?
verses.family_discussion: As a parent, what does it feel like to think about the long-term fruit of consistent, loving discipline? What keeps us going when it is hard?
verses.do_it_today: Thank a parent or teacher who has taken the time to correct and teach you.
verses.illustration_prompt: A parent and grown child embracing joyfully, warm light, a sense of peace and accomplishment, earlier discipline tools set aside, golden watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Where there is no vision, the people perish: but he that keepeth the law, happy is he.
verses.little_bible: Where God's Word is not taught, people fall apart and go wrong. But the person who obeys God's law is truly happy.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Where God's Word is not taught, people go wrong.
verses.meaning: The 'vision' here is not personal ambition or an organisation's mission statement — it is prophetic revelation, the Word of God. Where Scripture is not preached, taught, and obeyed, people throw off restraint and society unravels. The second half is the positive answer: the one who keeps the law — who lives by God's Word — finds true happiness. This verse is a call to keep Scripture central in every home and community.
verses.prayer: God, help me hear and obey Your Word every day.
verses.discussion_question: What happens to people when they stop listening to God's Word?
verses.family_discussion: What does it look like practically to keep God's Word central in our home — not just on Sundays but every day?
verses.do_it_today: Read or listen to one part of the Bible today, even just one verse.
verses.illustration_prompt: A bright open Bible in the centre of a home with joyful family around it, contrasted with a dark empty room with no book in sight, gentle watercolour scene

verses.kjv: A servant will not be corrected by words: for though he understand he will not answer.
verses.little_bible: Some people will not change just because you tell them to. They hear the words but do not respond.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Some people hear correction but will not change.
verses.meaning: This verse observes a hard truth about human nature: hearing is not the same as obeying. There are people who understand correction perfectly well and choose not to respond to it. For parents and leaders, this is a reminder that words alone are not always sufficient — authority, structure, and consistent consequences are also needed to shape behaviour.
verses.prayer: God, help me not just hear You but obey You.
verses.discussion_question: What is the difference between hearing something and actually changing?
verses.family_discussion: How do we create an environment where our children move from merely hearing instruction to genuinely internalising and obeying it?
verses.do_it_today: Think of something you know you should do but have not done yet. Do it today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A figure hearing words floating past them but doing nothing, an older wise person looking gently but seriously at them, subtle watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? there is more hope of a fool than of him.
verses.little_bible: Do you see someone who speaks too fast without thinking? A foolish person has more hope than they do.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Speaking without thinking is worse than being a fool.
verses.meaning: Hasty speech is treated as one of the most dangerous character flaws in Proverbs. The person who speaks without thinking, without listening, without weighing their words is harder to help than an outright fool — at least the fool's problem is obvious. The hasty speaker may not even know they have a problem. James 1:19 and Proverbs 18:13 echo this same warning.
verses.prayer: God, guard my mouth and slow my words.
verses.discussion_question: Why is speaking too quickly without thinking so dangerous?
verses.family_discussion: How do we model for our children the discipline of pausing — in conversation, in conflict, in emotion — before words are spoken that cannot be taken back?
verses.do_it_today: Before every answer you give today, count to three in your head first.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child with wide open mouth and a stream of words tumbling out too fast, a wise elder with finger to lips gently saying wait, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: He that delicately bringeth up his servant from a child shall have him become his son at the length.
verses.little_bible: If you always treat someone with too much softness and no correction, they will one day act like they own you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Too much softness without discipline causes problems later.
verses.meaning: Over-indulgence — raising someone (child or servant) with comfort but no correction, boundaries, or discipline — produces a person who eventually acts as though they have the rights of a superior. Kindness without structure is not kindness; it is a failure to prepare someone for life. True care includes both warmth and appropriate boundaries.
verses.prayer: God, help me receive both love and correction from others.
verses.discussion_question: What can go wrong if someone is always treated with softness but never corrected?
verses.family_discussion: How do we hold together genuine warmth and love for our children with the firm structure and discipline they need to become trustworthy and grounded adults?
verses.do_it_today: Ask a trusted adult: 'Is there something I need to be better at?' And really listen to the answer.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child being given everything with no boundaries, growing up looking spoiled and demanding, a gentle caring adult looking on with concern, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: An angry man stirreth up strife, and a furious man aboundeth in transgression.
verses.little_bible: An angry person causes fights everywhere they go. A furious person keeps doing wrong again and again.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Angry people cause trouble and keep doing wrong.
verses.meaning: Anger is not just an emotion — it is a force that creates conflict wherever it goes. The angry person stirs up strife; the furious person multiplies their own wrongdoing because uncontrolled anger leads to more and more sin. Anger is not forbidden in Scripture (God gets angry), but human anger must be governed, or it becomes destructive.
verses.prayer: God, help me control my anger.
verses.discussion_question: How does an angry person affect everyone around them?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to feel anger without letting anger control them — pointing them to God who is slow to anger and full of grace?
verses.do_it_today: The next time you feel angry, stop before you act. Take three deep breaths and pray.
verses.illustration_prompt: A furious figure with fire around them causing everyone nearby to scatter and argue, a calm figure standing peacefully at the edge, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: A man's pride shall bring him low: but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit.
verses.little_bible: Pride pulls a person down. But a humble spirit is lifted up and honoured.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Pride brings you down. Being humble lifts you up.
verses.meaning: Pride and humility have opposite trajectories. The proud person is on a downward path — God opposes the proud (James 4:6, 1 Peter 5:5). The humble person is upheld — sustained, honoured, and lifted. This is not just a social observation but a theological statement about how God relates to human hearts.
verses.prayer: God, keep me humble and lift me up in Your time.
verses.discussion_question: What is the difference between being proud and being humble?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate genuine humility in our children — not false modesty, but a true low opinion of their own importance compared to God and others?
verses.do_it_today: Let someone else go first today. Cheer for someone else's success instead of your own.
verses.illustration_prompt: A proud figure on a pedestal crumbling and falling, a humble child kneeling and being gently lifted up by a kind hand from above, warm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Whoso is partner with a thief hateth his own soul: he heareth cursing, and bewrayeth it not.
verses.little_bible: Joining in with someone who steals is hurting yourself. You hear the curse that comes with it, and you share it.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Joining a thief brings harm to yourself too.
verses.meaning: Being a partner in theft is self-destructive — the person hates their own soul by participating. The legal and spiritual consequences of complicity fall on everyone involved. In ancient law, a witness who heard cursing (a public oath to tell the truth) and stayed silent to protect a thief became guilty themselves. Partnership in wrongdoing is never neutral — it always implicates the partner.
verses.prayer: God, help me never join in with those doing wrong.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it harmful to join in when someone else is doing wrong?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that going along with someone else's wrongdoing — even silently — makes them responsible too?
verses.do_it_today: Refuse to join in if a friend wants to do something you know is wrong today.
verses.illustration_prompt: Two figures together taking something that does not belong to them, both looking guilty and troubled, warning light overhead, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the LORD shall be safe.
verses.little_bible: Worrying too much about what people think is a trap. But trusting God keeps you safe.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Trust God, not people, to keep you safe.
verses.meaning: The 'fear of man' is the controlling anxiety about what others think, say, or do to us — it causes people to lie, compromise, and disobey God to avoid human disapproval. This is one of the most common spiritual traps. The antidote is not fearlessness in oneself but trust in the LORD — the one whose opinion is final and whose protection is real.
verses.prayer: God, help me trust You more than I fear people.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to care too much about what people think?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children identify when they are making decisions out of fear of others rather than trust in God — and redirect them toward God's opinion as the one that matters?
verses.do_it_today: Think of something you have been afraid to do because of what people might think. Talk to God about it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child caught in a net of people's opinions and stares, contrasted with another child standing free and secure in golden light reaching up to God, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Many seek the ruler's favour; but every man's judgment cometh from the LORD.
verses.little_bible: Many people try to get the ruler's approval. But in the end, God is the true judge of every person.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: People chase leaders' approval, but God is the true judge.
verses.meaning: People expend enormous energy seeking favour from those in power. But human favour is fickle, limited, and ultimately irrelevant — because every person's final judgment comes from the LORD, not from any earthly ruler. This verse liberates us from people-pleasing and calls us to live for an audience of One.
verses.prayer: God, help me live to please You, not people.
verses.discussion_question: Why is God's opinion more important than a ruler's opinion?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children — who will spend their lives in environments that reward human approval — keep God's judgment as the standard that actually matters?
verses.do_it_today: Ask yourself: 'Am I doing this for God or for people?' Be honest with your answer.
verses.illustration_prompt: Many figures crowding around a throne seeking favour, but God's light shining above all of them as the true and final authority, warm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: An unjust man is an abomination to the just: and he that is upright in the way is abomination to the wicked.
verses.little_bible: Good people and wicked people cannot truly get along. Each finds the other deeply wrong.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Good and evil are truly opposites — they do not fit together.
verses.meaning: The chapter closes with a statement of moral and spiritual incompatibility. The just and the unjust are not simply different — they are, to each other, an abomination. Righteousness and wickedness are not two points on a spectrum; they are opposing forces. This does not mean the righteous should be cruel to sinners, but it does mean that there is no neutral ground between the way of the LORD and the way of the wicked.
verses.memory_phrase: Good and evil oppose each other.
verses.prayer: God, help me always choose the side of what is right.
verses.discussion_question: Why can good and evil not truly be friends?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children hold together genuine love for all people (as image-bearers) with a clear moral commitment that does not compromise righteousness?
verses.do_it_today: Choose one area today where you will clearly stand for what is right, even if it is hard.
verses.illustration_prompt: Two figures standing on opposite sides of a deep divide, light surrounding one and shadow the other, looking at each other with solemn expressions, watercolour scene
